audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed penultimate primary, alternating secondaries leftward = right-aligned syllabic trochees) rests on the standard reference grammar (Lynch 2000, PL 507, §2.5), which we hold in full and whose deciding sentence I confirmed verbatim on p. 24. Glottolog lists nothing fuller; the other descriptive items are Lynch's own shorter sketches (1982 downloaded now, confirms; 2002 print-only) and Inglis 1882. No instrumental or later phonological study surfaced in web search. One substantive note for the coders rather than a reclassify: Lynch describes a regular, segmentally conditioned antepenultimate primary stress (words .VCVCV(C)# with identical antepenult/penult vowels, or with /h/ as one of the single intervening consonants, pp. 25-26, rule 39) and surface-final stress on geminate (long) final vowels (underlyingly penultimate). sources.quote: "Generally, primary stress in Anejom appears to fall on the penultimate syllable, with geminate vowels counting as two syllables ... There is some evidence, however, that primary stress falls on the antepenultimate syllable if the antepenultimate and penultimate syllables of a word contain the same vocalic elements and are separated by a single consonant ... Stress is, however, one more area of Anejom phonology that requires considerably more attention."
